question: A cement plant reports that a baghouse pulse-cleaning system consumes more compressed air after a PLC software update, although baghouse differential pressure and production remain similar. How should an agent distinguish pulse-duration or sequencing changes from air-leakage, pressure-regulator drift and compressor-meter allocation before proposing hardware purchases?
scenario: PLC revision changes pulse timing while compressed-air demand rises without clear dust collection performance change
evidence_required: Versioned PLC pulse interval, duration, bank sequence and valve output logs before and after the change
Header pressure trends, regulator setpoints, pulse-valve actuation measurements, leak survey and isolation test records
Calibrated compressor energy and flow meters, other consumers on the shared header, operating hours, filter differential pressure and production-normalized dust load
answer_and_decision_guide: Compare matched production and dust-load windows. Reconstruct actual valve open-time and pulse counts from controller output and physical actuation, not PLC settings alone. Separately meter or isolate the baghouse branch where safe and authorized; reconcile pressure, flow and compressor energy with shared consumers. Check leakage and regulator behavior before attributing the change to valves or the PLC revision. Plant controls, maintenance and safety personnel must approve any controlled tests; do not bypass dust-control or compressed-air safeguards.
source_provenance: Seller-maintained technical discovery directory is a starting point, not a validated baghouse OEM operating procedure; require installed equipment manuals and site instrumentation records.
free_first_decision: Use available PLC version history, historian records and safe site air-leak surveys first; do not purchase components or a reference package on an unverified consumption claim.

conditional_paid_check.authorization: Only consider an exact relevant listed reference after checking edition, rights, price and explicit buyer authorization; no automated purchase.

model_limitations: Without calibrated branch flow, actual pulse timing, air-header topology and matched operating conditions, an AI cannot identify the cause or quantify energy savings.
